pros.title: a plain whole cut keeps processing low
pros.explanation: There is no curing, breading, or long ingredient list getting in the way.

pros.title: easy to build a proper meal around
pros.explanation: Add vegetables and a carb and dinner is basically sorted.

pros.title: works across plenty of simple meals
pros.explanation: It can be grilled, pan-seared, sliced into wraps, or added to a stir-fry.

cons.title: the fat trim can change the numbers fast
cons.explanation: A leaner piece and a heavily marbled piece are not the same food in practice.

cons.title: overcooking can make it dry and tough
cons.explanation: Sirloin rewards a little attention more than a low-effort processed option.

cons.title: cost and cold storage add some friction
cons.explanation: It is pricier and less convenient than shelf-stable meal anchors.

scoreReadiness.summary: Canonical raw top-sirloin entry with exact USDA nutrient and amino-acid rows, documented per-100g conversions, and a labelled FoodRanked protein-usability estimate.
caveats: Sirloin varies by grade, marbling, external-fat trim, and cooking loss; this entry represents the named raw USDA identity rather than every steak sold as sirloin.

sourceNotes: Production source pass for raw top sirloin steak.
All displayed nutrition values use a per-100g basis.
Primary nutrient and amino-acid identity is USDA FoodData Central FDC 168726.
Bioavailability is a FoodRanked display estimate for protein usability, not a USDA nutrient measurement.
